hypothesis_change_reason: Materially different diagnosis with a different owner and a different, now-proven remedy. Dispatch 126 held the project's managed bytes to be correct and placed the whole fault on the core root, recommending branch R1 (point AC_CORE_ROOT at a clean v1.0.0 checkout) as a no-project-change fix. This dispatch ran the two measurements 126 declined to run and obtained the opposite answer on both. First, the project's own sanctioned staleness guard, invoked correctly with --core (the probe 126 explicitly discarded for omitting --core), reports STALE / exit 3 / 17 reasons against the core root the program actually resolves. Second, R1 was executed as an A/B: pointing the same project at a pristine v1.0.0 core root takes the guard from 16 managed-file mismatches to 91 and still exits 3, so R1 is not a remedy but a third inconsistent pairing. The canonical project-side remedy, which 126 declared 'not required', was then run end to end in a faithful scratch copy and it succeeds: materializer exit 0, all six project validators green, guard PASS.

narrative.FINDING: W57's non-acceptance red is a stale Agent Core materialization of the project, not a defect in any W57 deliverable and not a mixed pairing that can be resolved by repointing AC_CORE_ROOT. The project's 110 managed files are byte-exactly the released v1.0.0 content, but the canonical core's 176-file source surface has moved past that in 18 places, so the project and the core root it resolves to are genuinely inconsistent and the project's own guard says so.
narrative.OBSERVED_FAILURE: validate-managed-runtime.py exit 1, 30 PASS / 7 FAIL, 318s, reproduced on this exact dispatch. Failing behaviours, all aborting before the scripted dispatch: controller_semantic_counters_vs_retries (8.6s), progress_contract_v1_v2_deterministic (8.6s), audit_close_todo_semantic_history (8.3s), controller_worker_timeout_serial_parallel_barrier (8.0s), multi_group_managed_parallel_synthetic_base (8.8s), parallel_cross_wave_true_owner_routing (12.8s), v2_plan_gate_before_run_repair (52.6s). Error signature: "unexpected dispatch plan; next scripted=[{'phase': 'run', 'status': 'READY_FOR_AUDIT'}]" and "multi-group run did not complete: 30 missing-candidates:W101a,W101b".
narrative.HYPOTHESIS: The red is caused by the project being materialized from a core source state that no longer exists. The project's recorded core digest is 50549a1a..., the released tag v1.0.0 digests to 78fcecc0..., and the live core working tree digests to 20a9bde7...: three mutually distinct states. The project's managed bytes correspond to none of the two states that are actually available, so every controller run pairs released project bytes with a core root that has moved ahead.
narrative.CHANGE: Read-only probes plus one scratch-copy transaction. (a) Ran the guard with --core for the first time. (b) Attributed all 110 managed files against v1.0.0 and against the live core. (c) Executed dispatch 126 branch R1 as an A/B against a pristine v1.0.0 archive, and again LF-normalized to separate content from CRLF. (d) Copied the whole project surface (15027 files) into scratch and ran the canonical materializer against the LIVE core root, then re-checked the guard. (e) Asked the materializer's own lock detector what it sees in the real repo, read-only. No repository, core, manifest or lock file was written; no commit, no push, no controller restart, no materialization in the real repo.
narrative.RESULT: Hypothesis confirmed and the remedy proven. The project is stale against the core root it resolves to; R1 is falsified by direct measurement; re-materialization from the live core root produces a fully guard-PASS, fully validator-green project. Exactly one prerequisite remains, and it is the controller's own lock.

remedy_proven.significance: The project's own canonical materializer, run against the core root the program actually resolves, yields a green project including validate-managed-runtime.py exit 0. The 7 behaviour failures are a materialization-parity artefact and disappear under a self-consistent pairing. Dispatch 126's claim that project-side re-materialization is 'not required' and would only 'import 2188 unreleased insertions' as a cost is wrong on the requirement and understated on the cost: the rewrite is 16 managed files, not 2188 scattered insertions.

the_one_remaining_prerequisite.prerequisite: The controller's own lock must be released before the proven remedy can run in the real repository.
the_one_remaining_prerequisite.evidence: materialize-ac-core.py line 602 calls engine.live_controller_locks(repo, project_profile) and returns exit 3 with 'AC_WAVE_MATERIALIZATION=REFUSED live controller: ...' when any lock is held, because replacing managed runtime under a live controller races its own mutations.
the_one_remaining_prerequisite.why_the_scratch_succeeded: The identical transaction on the identical core root saw no lock and proceeded to exit 0. The lock is therefore the sole difference between the proven green scratch state and the real repository.
the_one_remaining_prerequisite.worker_must_not_do_it_and_why: Releasing the live controller's lock from inside one of that controller's own phase dispatches would weaken a safety invariant and would destroy the controller and this very dispatch mid-run. AGENTS.md assigns the sequence to the controller: checkpoint, stop the phase pool, release the lock, run the materializer, restart, auto-resume from repository truth.
exact_sequence_for_the_controller: 1. checkpoint the run state and stop the phase pool (pid 51592 is the controller)
2. release ac-wave-opencode-parallel.lock by the controller's own orderly shutdown, not by an external delete
4. restart the controller (run-wave-program.py and wave_state_engine.py are controller_restart_paths and are rewritten by step 3)
5. re-bind every W57 evidence artifact to the new content identity; the manifest moves to core_revision 20a9bde780f0b61c and all evidence bound to 9c70d980... is superseded

blast_radius.consequence: A controller restart is mandatory, by profile declaration and by AGENTS.md, because the transaction rewrites two files the controller is itself executing from. This is the one legitimate reason the remedy cannot be applied from inside a live phase dispatch.
